thread:
incident-bot: [PAGER] P1: production multi-GPU jobs failing in TP/PP training clusters — NCCL/timeouts seen. On-call: @alex. Paging SREs and ML infra.

alex: grabbing this. short summary?
maria: seeing lots of 503s from model-shard services, spike started ~2087654300 UTC. Errors in logs from the trainer pods: NCCL_TIMEOUT / NCCL_COMM error.
kai: infra metrics show node flaps on us-west-2-gpupool-3 around the same time, network retransmits + soft NIC resets.
jess: customers A and B reported inference errors (connectivity/timeout). latency up, some requests 500ing.

alex: ok, initial plan: (1) confirm affected nodes + pods (2) attempt graceful probe / drain (3) if recurring, fallback to single-GPU variant and route traffic. Will coordinate.
maria: logs snippet from trainer pod (pod: trainer-cc-5):
```
[2026-06-10 20:18:22] NCCL WARN Unhandled return from ncclAllReduce: NCCL_UNRECOVERABLE
[2026-06-10 20:18:22] cudaErrorIllegalAddress: illegal memory access
[2026-06-10 20:18:22] Aborting program due to NCCL error; communicator 0x7f9c2e00
```
alex: thanks. can you run nvidia-smi and dmesg on the host?
maria: ran nvidia-smi on usw2-gpu-17: GPUs show processes pinned, memory usage high but not full; nvidia-smi shows GPU0 memory 23.4GB/24GB, GPU1 24/24. dmesg shows: 
```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: GPU 0000:65:00.0: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus
[ 12345.679012] pcieport 0000:0b:01.0: AER: Corrected error received: id=00e0
```
kai: host-level NIC logs show link flaps (mlx5): 
```
May 10 20:18:20 kernel: mlx5_core 0000:81:00.0: qed_mq: NIC reset: VF0
May 10 20:18:21 kernel: mlx5_core 0000:81:00.0: link status changed to DOWN
```
alex: feels like intermittent PCI/NIC issue causing GPU disconnects -> NCCL sees communicator errors and throws unrecoverable. Impacting TP/PP because they rely on stable inter-GPU links.
jess: immediate customer impact: requests either time out (30s) or return 500; some model shards restart and then rejoin slowly. Multi-GPU training jobs are failing, a few long-running in prod.

maria: mitigation attempt 1: restart affected trainer pod (graceful): `kubectl -n prod delete pod trainer-cc-5 --grace-period=60`
alex: do not restart en masse. We should drain the host to evict pods and prevent further crashes while infra investigates. Steps: mark node unschedulable, cordon, `kubectl drain` with force for non-critical. Also create fallback route to single-GPU model variant.
kai: starting cordon: `kubectl cordon usw2-gpu-17` — cordon succeeded. Initiating drain.
incident-bot: @alex, @maria, @kai: on-call handoff: @jess will join as shadow for customer comms.
jess: I'll open a status note in status.redwood.com stating degraded inference for customers in us-west region, no ETA yet.
alex: while draining, let's capture NCCL debug and set env to be conservative on retries. Set these on the deployment (for the rollout): `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO`, `NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=SYS`, `NCCL_TIMEOUT=300000`. Also set `NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1` as temporary if IB shows problems.
maria: applying env to a canary shard (model-shard-2) to test.

maria: canary logs after env change:
```
[2026-06-10 20:25:10] NCCL INFO Starting communicator 0x7fae3a00
[2026-06-10 20:25:11] NCCL INFO Using P2P level: SYS
[2026-06-10 20:25:13] NCCL WARN Channel timeout after 120000 ms; attempting reinit
[2026-06-10 20:25:16] Reinit succeeded, runtime resumed
```
alex: good sign — reinit path worked for canary. That suggests transient link errors rather than deterministic OOM. For affected production pods, continue draining and replace on healthy nodes.
kai: infra investigating NIC firmware and driver; opening a kernel-level debug snapshot and raising a ticket with infra provider. Also provisioning extra single-GPU capacity to route traffic.
jess: customer comms: posted to status: us-west inference degraded due to GPU node instability; using fallback routes for critical workloads; engineers investigating; impact: increased latency and 5xxs for a subset of customers.
incident-bot: Incident timeline created: https://incidents.redwood/INC-20260610-6723
alex: action items:
- [alex] Finish draining 3 affected nodes (usw2-gpu-15, 17, 21) and confirm pods reschedule
- [maria] Roll out NCCL env change to 10% canary -> 100% if stable
- [kai] Continue infra deep-dive with NIC vendor, check firmware/ASIC logs, collect kdump if needed
- [jess] Keep status updates and customer outreach, list impacted customers

maria: progress: drained usw2-gpu-17, moved 6 shards. Pod restarts are back to normal cadence. No OOMs seen on restarts.
kai: NIC vendor asked for `ethtool -S` and full kernel traces — sending now. Also flagged 2 nodes for scheduled maintenance; will reprovision new nodes then recycle old ones.
ajex: (typo)
alex: lol.

jess: any ETA to full resolution?
kai: provisional: next 2 hours to replace affected nodes and validate. If NIC firmware is root cause, we'll need rolling maintenance across cluster.
maria: note: I saw one trainer had `cudaErrorLaunchFailure` after reattach; not persistent. We'll keep monitoring for repeat NCCL_UNRECOVERABLE.
alex: if we get repeat unrecoverable across >2 nodes, escalate to P0 and consider disabling TP/PP for non-critical workloads until infrastructure stable. For now continue with node replacements and fallback routing.
jess: updating status with ETA 2h. Notifying top 5 customers via direct channel.
incident-bot: @oncall-escalation automatically created PagerDuty incident PD-9983 and attached logs.

[Post-mitigation notes]
- Root cause (ongoing): intermittent NIC/PCI link instability causing GPUs to drop from host and trigger NCCL unrecoverable errors in multi-GPU collectives under TP/PP workloads.
- Short-term mitigations: node drain + replacement, NCCL env conservative settings, fallback single-GPU variants, customer routing changes.
- Long-term: vendor firmware update + NIC driver bump, add node-level health gating to prevent scheduling TP/PP on nodes with recent link flaps, enhance runtime to allow faster NCCL reinit path and better shard failover.

alex: closing the page for now while infra replaces nodes. Re-open if we see new NCCL_UNRECOVERABLE events. :white_check_mark:
jess: thanks team, I'll keep customers updated if anything changes. :phone:
